title: Draft: Qt: Refactor Expert Info model with unlimited capacity design
description:
This change replaces the current O(n) store for expert information, with
a flat model for easier storage and around a 10th of the original storage
size. 

Additionally all the grouping is done in the proxy model, allowing also
for different grouping modes (by protocol, severity, ...)

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)

Fixes #20970

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • f88567d4 - Remove doc file
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23360/diffs?diff_id=1638758237&start_sha=51cc9e22d2c28f8a2c60d0e8c1776596d3f8a4b4)
I think the design looks cleaner here than the existing. I'll work at instrumenting it.

I created some sample files with lots of the same Expert Info using that script provided by the person who opened the issue. Using Callgrind, I can turn on instrumentation only in `cf_retap_packets`. The calls from that are split into two groups, one for dissections plus pushing the tap queue from `retap_packet`, and one for GUI updates from `update_progress_dlg`. The `retap_packet` group can be split into two subgroups, one for just the dissections in `dissect_record`, and one for the tapping `tap_push_tapped_queue` which is almost entirely `ExpertInfoModel::tapPacket`.

I built a Debug build and a Release build with GCC for the this MR and the current master branch after my patch.

|  | dissect_record | tapPacket | retap_packet | tapDraw | cf_retap_packet |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| master 50k Debug      | ` 3071273336` | `1201821631` | ` 4366990830` | `  288336370` | ` 4955906975` |
| master 100k Debug     | ` 6138194755` | `2401668873` | ` 8728321097` | `  786045387` | `10009087603` |
| master 200k Debug     | `12271932893` | `4839555306` | `17498285338` | ` 3020522014` | `21362203835` |
| refactor 50k Debug    | ` 3075347910` | ` 750463358` | ` 3919612840` | `  820163462` | ` 5017362728` |
| refactor 100k Debug   | ` 6156447048` | `1496202623` | ` 7840253827` | ` 3263021895` | `11753418057` |
| refactor 200k Debug   | `12283891784` | `2990711446` | `15649813805` | `20549180307` | `37496970829` |
| master 50k Release    | ` 1620435154` | ` 695955527` | ` 2381140037` | `     125411` | ` 2868244299` |
| master 100k Release   | ` 3243003026` | `1397250009` | ` 4770052653` | `     190763` | ` 5394034419` |
| master 200k Release   | ` 6499427773` | `2838601433` | ` 9604035871` | `     324644` | `10433613363` |
| refactor 50k Release  | ` 1621559691` | ` 178323498` | ` 1864384595` | `  125131840` | ` 2378087491` |
| refactor 100k Release | ` 3240636467` | ` 354892841` | ` 3724530816` | `  421584996` | ` 4622255140` |
| refactor 200k Release | ` 6477398388` | ` 704120548` | ` 7439527628` | ` 1655136865` | ` 9848426949` |

This is with not trying to expand any of the QTreeView rows while the retapping is going on; since the model completely resets (I suppose `layoutChanged()` could be used instead of `modelReset()`) there's little point in expanding the rows because the selections will all go away each time the model resets. The current master hack would probably be worse with expanding the rows, whereas this refactor would probably not be affected as much.

The counts from `retap_packet` are perfectly linear with the number of packets (since these frames have identical payload) and don't vary between the two approaches, as expected. It is included as it's part of the overall time for the dialog to process and provides a good sense of how much a percentage of the time the tapping is as opposed to dissection.

As you can see, this refactor is considerably more efficient in tapPacket (storing the information in the model) at the expense of considerably more work in tapDraw (resetting the model so that the GUI catches up.) Somewhat concerning is that the time taken in tapDraw appears to increase at O(N^2) in the refactor.
Thank you very much for the analysis. Let's see how we can improve tapDraw further. What is considerably smaller though is the memory consumption. Have you tried that as well?
I haven't taken detailed measurements of the memory, but just by inspection it does look like the memory consumption would be much better, I agree.

There's probably some other ways to do it that may or may not look uglier, like using a QHash<unsigned, qsizetype> instead of QStrings for the hash keys when grouping by severity or other number-like types.
Qt5 requires `#include <QSet>` here. It's not needed for Qt6, but doesn't really hurt.
This ends up being very expensive because it's called many times. There's only a few possible severities, so storing them as literals would make a big difference.
tbh, I am currently rethinking the approach. It is overall quite messy. Not sure if it will be in time for 5.0 though

commits_data.title: Qt: Implement ExpertInfoGroupingProxyModel with lookup-table
commits_data.message:
Qt: Implement ExpertInfoGroupingProxyModel with lookup-table

- Rewrite proxy model to use unlimited capacity lookup table
- Add clear() method to ExpertInfoModel
- Track severity counts in addEntry()
- Implement all QAbstractProxyModel methods
- Support multiple grouping modes (severity, protocol, group, summary)

Fixes: #20970

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)

commits_data.title: Qt: Refactor Expert Info model with unlimited capacity design
commits_data.message:
Qt: Refactor Expert Info model with unlimited capacity design

- Replace bit-packing ID encoding with lookup-table approach
- Add ProxyEntry struct for O(1) index lookups
- Update GroupNode to use qsizetype for unlimited capacity
- Add INVALID_ENTRY_ID sentinel for group header detection
- Document new architecture in README.expert_info_model
